title: LoRAX docs: Medusa (adapters guide)
quote: When using a v2 Medusa adapter as default, you can also apply per-request Medusa adapters (that must also be v2) to specialize the speculative decoding to the particular task.
proves: LoRAX (since May 2024) serves per-request, dynamically loaded speculation adapters (Medusa v2 sharing the base LM head) alongside per-request LoRAs in one batch; doc claims ~50% gain for a general Medusa vs ~100% for a task-specific one.
does_not_prove: Pairing of a LoRA with its own Medusa heads was only planned ('In the future, we also plan to support LoRAs that come with their own Medusa heads'); no accept-length table vs number of adapters; vendor claim, no paper.
bearing: Kills novelty of C6 per-adapter drafter adapters co-batched

title: LoRAX docs: Speculative Decoding guide
quote: LoRAX implements some of these approaches, with a particular emphasis on supporting adapter-based methods like Medusa that can be applied per request for task-level speedups.
proves: A production multi-LoRA server designed speculation around per-request adapter-based drafters; prompt lookup is not compatible with per-request Medusa adapters.
does_not_prove: No measurement of draft-adapter memory or kernel cost at 10-100 adapters.

title: predibase/lorax repository (archived)
quote: packs requests for different adapters together into the same batch
proves: LoRAX does heterogeneous continuous batching of adapters; the repo was archived on Oct 12, 2026 (read-only).
does_not_prove: Page itself says nothing about speculation; archive means no maintained baseline.
bearing: Prior art for C6; baseline availability risk

title: Speculative Streaming: Efficient and Scalable Speculative Decoding with Multi-Stream Attention
quote: In such systems, a dedicated draft model or Medusa heads are typically required for each downstream application to obtain high acceptance rates, resulting in substantial cumulative memory overhead.
proves: Apple frames per-application drafters on a LoRA-adapted shared base as a known memory problem (Medusa: 1.2 GB per app, 11.8 GB at 10 apps on Llama-2-7B) and proposes per-application shared adapters that fuse drafting into the target, ~1000x fewer extra params than Medusa.
does_not_prove: On-device, one application at a time; no batched multi-adapter serving, no co-batching of different applications' draft adapters.
bearing: Weakens novelty of C6 per-adapter draft parameters

title: [Feature]: Reduce LoRA latency via speculative decoding (vLLM #6912)
quote: Note this work does not include applying LoRA to the speculator; that can be a future work.
proves: vLLM named speculator-side LoRA as future work in July 2024; still not upstream in Oct 2026 (RFC L201 open).
bearing: C6 relevance: known gap for 2+ years, engineering backlog

title: [Bug]: LoRA + Gemma4 MTP speculative decoding crashes at startup (vLLM #62340)
quote: Enabling LoRA on Gemma-4 with MTP speculative decoding crashes the engine at startup during memory profiling.
proves: As of 2026-10-18 LoRA+MTP still breaks in vLLM for Gemma4 because the drafter takes a placeholder embed instead of the shared one when LoRA is on.
bearing: C6: LoRA+spec is still at correctness-bug stage, so baseline is shaky

title: AFA-LoRA: Enabling Non-Linear Adaptations in LoRA with Activation Function Annealing
quote: We implement our method on supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and speculative decoding.
proves: LoRA-style training is applied to speculative-decoding drafters (abstract).
does_not_prove: Single adapter; abstract gives no serving, multi-adapter, or per-tenant drafting result.
bearing: Weak prior art for C6 draft LoRA

title: Accepted Prefixes Are Not All You Need: A Negative Result on PEFT-Based Block-Diffusion Drafting
quote: the drafter is parameter-efficient but not compute-efficient.
proves: A LoRA-like adapter used as a block-diffusion drafter on the verifier's own backbone gives no practical speedup on Qwen3-0.6B.
does_not_prove: Applies to self-drafting adapters on the full backbone, not to a LoRA on a small separate drafter.
bearing: Negative result bounding C6's self-adapter variant (Uno-like)

title: Serving Heterogeneous LoRA Adapters in Distributed LLM Inference Systems (LoRAServe)
quote: Serving Heterogeneous LoRA Adapters in Distributed LLM Inference Systems
proves: Rank-heterogeneous co-batching of adapters causes performance skew; adapter placement/routing gives up to 2x throughput, 9x lower TTFT on production traces.
does_not_prove: Never mentions speculative decoding or drafters.
bearing: C6 adjacent: multi-adapter placement is solved without speculation

title: ADP Balance Strategy (TensorRT-LLM tech blog 10)
quote: The execution time for the Attention module in any given iteration is bounded by the rank with the highest workload.
proves: On DeepSeek V3, DP=8 attention + EP=8, baseline average balance ratio is 54.11%; delaying context (prefill) admission raises it to 87.70% and TPS 1.33x. Imbalance is driven by context tasks.
does_not_prove: Does not say whether MTP was on; no acceptance or draft-token discussion.
bearing: C7 Scale/Oracle: prefill admission, not acceptance, dominates DP imbalance

title: DeepSeek-V4-Pro on vLLM recipe
quote: Tune K and the prefill/decode (PD) ratio for each target concurrency
proves: Production DEP recipe (DP 8 + EP, DSpark K=5-6) uses one static K per deployment and balances DP ranks by prefill admission interval only.
does_not_prove: No acceptance-aware or per-rank-K balancing measured or discussed.
bearing: C7 relevance: production uses static K under DP; no demand signal for per-rank K

title: DSD: A Distributed Speculative Decoding Solution for Edge-Cloud Agile Large Model Serving
quote: extends SD to multi-device deployments through coordinated draft-target execution
proves: Distributed draft/target execution with a simulator and adaptive window control.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not describe acceptance-aware request routing across ranks.

title: Cascadia: A Control-Plane-Free Alternative to Hyperconverged AI Infrastructure
proves: Replica routing uses capability, load, in-flight count and peer health; distributed spec decode exists alongside.
does_not_prove: Routing does not use acceptance rate.
bearing: C7: another router that ignores acceptance

title: AdaSpec: Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Fast, SLO-Aware Large Language Model Serving
quote: apply a uniform speculative length for all requests within a batch
proves: Per-request speculative length beats threshold-based (batch-level) dynamic speculation by 9-58%; e.g. trace 1: 1.16x vs 1.73x.
does_not_prove: Measures aggregate speedup, not cross-request harm or tenant isolation.
bearing: Kills C9 mechanism novelty (per-request vs batch-level control)

title: Token Latency Fairness: Performance Isolation for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving
quote: well-behaved clients can still experience significant degradation to their token-level latencies.
proves: Token-level multi-tenant isolation in decode is an active 2026 topic.
bearing: C9 adjacent: isolation framing exists without speculation

title: FusionML: Prefill, Not Decode - Mechanism and Boundaries of CPU+GPU Co-Execution on Unified-Memory Apple Silicon
quote: decode cannot benefit, bound by shared bandwidth co-execution does not add
proves: On Apple silicon, CPU+GPU co-execution speeds prefill 1.15-1.38x but leaves decode throughput unchanged because decode is bound by shared bandwidth.
does_not_prove: Operator splitting, not a CPU drafter; abstract only.
bearing: C10 negative: CPU work during decode competes for the same bandwidth

title: Lossless but Not Free: An Empirical Anatomy of Speculative Decoding on Consumer Hardware
quote: three of five configurations decelerate, either because the draft fails to out-speed a small target or because the quantized Metal backend executes
proves: On an Apple-silicon laptop 3 of 5 spec configs slow down; quantized Metal verification runs serially.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; no CPU n-gram overlap study.
bearing: C10: the Metal bottleneck is verification, not draft placement

title: Cross-Family Speculative Decoding for Polish Language Models on Apple Silicon (Bielik 11B, MLX-LM)
proves: Search snippet: on Apple silicon shared bus bandwidth (200 GB/s M2 Pro) is the ceiling for memory-bound draft and target.

title: Speculative Decoding for vLLM Inference Services (Alauda AI 2.8 docs)
quote: The proposer's CPU work, the verification of five candidate tokens per step, and the fact that vLLM disables async scheduling under N-gram together cost more than the accepted tokens save.
proves: Qwen3-8B on one A30: n-gram K=5 gives 0.98x on code refactor and 0.85x on chat.
does_not_prove: Does not separate CPU proposer time from verification cost; one vendor run.
bearing: C10: n-gram loss is dominated by verification and lost async, not draft time alone
